root_cause_criterion.criterion: After DataValue_copy error cleanup returns from DataValue_clear(dst, NULL), the nested DataValue-array field dst->value.data must already be NULL if that cleanup freed it; otherwise the caller can immediately re-clear the same destination through a stale array pointer.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable Variant_clear frees p->data at src/ua_types.c:410 but leaves the caller-visible field dst->value.data unchanged through the first cleanup. The fixed program adds p->data = NULL at that free site, so the same DataValue_copy cleanup reaches UA_copy with dst->value.data cleared before the second UA_clear(dst, type).

nodes.state: The crashing Variant_clear call reads p->storageType from the first UA_DataValue element reached through the stale inner-array base pointer during the second cleanup walk.

edges.relation: The inner UA_DataValue-array pointer freed by the first cleanup is still stored in the same destination field when UA_copy enters its error-path UA_clear(dst, type), so the second clear reuses the freed array base.

The stale inner-array base used by the second clear becomes the owner object of the first UA_Variant cleared in that array walk, carrying the freed allocation directly into the crashing p->storageType read.
